To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Brian’s Monday brief: Embakasi pay and Kisumu loading, 30 November

Brian,

Thanks for taking this while I’m travelling. After six years working together, you know I wouldn’t leave you to walk into this with “please calm everyone down” and no answers. This is our mess, not theirs. The guys did nothing wrong. Go in with an apology and the facts, not a defence of management.

This is a draft for my review tonight. The timings below are a plan for Monday, not confirmation that money has already been sent.

What happened to Friday’s pay

Friday’s bank file covered 212 casuals. The bank rejected the entire file at 1:52pm because the beneficiary-reference field was longer than the new template allowed following its 25 November platform upgrade. No payments in that file were processed.

The rejection alert went to the old Finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, by which time the bank cut-off had passed. So this was a payment-file problem compounded by us missing the rejection in time to fix it. It was not caused by the casuals or their work, and the 14 unconfirmed phone numbers are not why Friday’s bank payment failed.

For the group, keep it simple: “Our payment file was rejected, and we didn’t pick up the rejection before the bank closed for processing. That is our failure. You worked and you should have been paid on Friday. I’m sorry.”

What is approved, and when payment is expected

Njeri has approved switching the affected payments to M-Pesa. She has also approved KES 500 for lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list, in the same M-Pesa batch. That is KES 500 total per person, not KES 500 for each item. The company bears the M-Pesa charges; they are not to be deducted from anyone’s pay.

Kevin’s current realistic estimate is Monday by 11am. That is the estimate we have, not a guaranteed receipt time. Approval is in place, but we do not yet have confirmation that the batch has been sent or that everyone’s phone details are ready.

Peninah has confirmed 198 numbers. She could not reach 14 people, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She will be at Embakasi from 7:30am with the list and a printout so those people can verify their numbers face to face. She is also bringing her laptop for anyone who wants a printed payslip. Handle number checks privately; don’t read people’s details out to the crowd.

Before Monday’s briefing, get Kevin’s latest position: is the batch ready, what still needs doing, and how will the 14 be handled once their numbers are checked? Ask whether the 198 can proceed separately if any of the remaining details take longer. Don’t present that as an agreed arrangement until he confirms it. In particular, don’t tell the 14 that giving Peninah a number at 7:30 guarantees payment by 11.

What you can promise — and what you cannot

You can confirm the approved payment route, the KES 500 addition for everyone affected, and that the company pays the M-Pesa charges. You can promise an in-person management apology, proper follow-up on missing payments, and updates even when there is no good news.

You cannot promise money before loading, before the 9am departure, “by lunch”, or at any other guaranteed hour. Say: “Finance’s current estimate is by 11am Monday. I will check and update you; I cannot honestly guarantee when it will show on each phone.”

Remember Mombasa in 2024: the supervisor said “by lunch”, the money arrived at 4pm and half the shift sat down. We are not doing that again. Joseph is already hearing that management previously said “tomorrow” for three days. Another confident deadline without confirmation will make this worse.

Do not offer cash advances, extra compensation or another payment arrangement that has not been approved. Do not make the KES 500 or the wages conditional on agreeing to load. And no threats about contracts, replacement or dismissal on Monday.

Before 6am: Ouma first

You’re there at 5:30. Find Joseph straight away and get the overnight picture. Ask him to help you speak privately with Ouma before everyone gathers. Ouma is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four children and rent to meet. Remember that when you speak to him; don’t use his family circumstances as pressure or mention them to the group.

Something like:

“Ouma, I wanted to speak to you before we address everyone. We let you down on Friday. I know people have commitments that couldn’t wait. I’m not asking you to pretend this is fine. Let me tell you exactly what is approved and what we still need to confirm, then I want to hear what the men are saying.”

Listen first. Ask him to help keep the discussion calm, but don’t expect him to guarantee everyone else’s cooperation or make him responsible for solving our mistake.

I’m up from 4:30. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes: payment timing, the mood at the depot, or a refusal to load. My flight leaves at 7:05, so don’t assume I’ll be reachable right up to 7 or once we’re airborne.

What to say to everyone

“Morning, everyone. First, I’m sorry. You did your work and your Friday pay did not arrive. Our bank file was rejected and we missed the rejection before the processing cut-off. That is on us, not you.

“Payment through M-Pesa has now been approved. Everyone on the affected list will also receive KES 500 for Monday lunch and fare in the same batch, and the company will cover the M-Pesa charges. Finance’s current estimate is by 11am. I am not going to give you a guaranteed hour that I cannot keep.

“Peninah will be here at 7:30 to check the numbers she couldn’t confirm and help with payslips. If your payment doesn’t arrive, we will follow up your case individually.

“I know the Kisumu trucks are due out at 9, before that payment estimate. I’m asking you to load while we resolve this, but I understand why you want to see the money first. I’ll give you another update at 8, even if the position hasn’t changed.”

Keep the 8am update: that is something you can control. Agree the next update time each time you speak.

If Ouma’s group refuses to load

The 9am departure is a real constraint: missing it means missing the mill’s offloading slot. But payment is currently expected later than departure. Do not suggest the two timings somehow line up, or that loading will make the money arrive sooner.

Ask calmly whether the group is refusing all loading or whether there is something they need clarified before deciding. Hear them out, with Ouma and a small number of representatives if that helps. Don’t argue across the yard or single anyone out publicly.

Our v3 procedure says a stoppage must be handled jointly by Operations and HR. You are the Operations lead, not both halves of that process. Before Monday, we need a named HR colleague confirmed to cover after I board, with their number in your hand. That cover is still to be settled in this draft. Peninah’s payroll visit is not automatically HR stoppage cover.

If loading stops, contact me while I’m available and bring the designated HR cover into the response. Keep Joseph involved, keep the loading area safe, and make a factual note of the time, what work has stopped, the concerns raised and the actions agreed. No dismissals and no threats of dismissal that day. No contract threats dressed up as advice.

The normal grievance route is supervisor first, then HR within 48 hours. The procedure says stoppages are not a grievance channel, but don’t lead with that as a warning. It does not remove our responsibility to hear the pay grievance or permit you to handle the stoppage alone.

For the trucks, establish early how much loading remains and the latest safe point at which a 9am departure is still possible. If refusal or delay puts that at risk, escalate to Njeri and the transport team immediately; don’t wait until 9 to report it. Ask transport to establish the options with the mill for a delayed arrival or another slot. Those are contingency enquiries, not promises that a new slot exists. Do not rush unsafe loading or use colleagues who are willing to work as a threat against those who aren’t.

At 11am, check receipts, not just whether Finance says “sent”. If payments are missing, get Kevin and Peninah to trace them and give the affected people an honest update. If the estimate has slipped, say so plainly and give a next update time, not another invented payment deadline.

For tonight’s review, the two gaps to close are Kevin’s latest processing position, including the 14 numbers, and named HR cover after I board. The apology and the approved support are clear. The exact receipt time is not.

Achieng
